0.text: A referral from a friend never does.

1.text: 92 percent of consumers trust recommendations from friends and family more than any form of advertising.
That's from Nielsen's Global Trust in Advertising study.
No ad budget, no social post
and no Google ranking comes close to that level of trust before the first conversation even happens.

2.text: Referred customers are 4 times more likely to refer others themselves.
One strong referral can generate another, and another.
Businesses that consistently generate referrals are not doing anything complicated.
They are just not leaving the ask on the table.

3.text: The gap between a personal recommendation and any other marketing channel is massive.
92 percent versus 39 percent for social ads.
Trust is what closes sales before the conversation even starts.
No other channel produces that kind of advantage for free.

4.text: Referred customers have a 37 percent higher retention rate than customers you find through cold marketing.
Trust takes time to build from scratch, but it comes pre-installed with a referral.

5.text: A referred customer's average lifetime value is 16 percent higher than a non-referred one.
They buy more, stay longer, and cost nothing to find.
It is a trust premium that compounds over the life of the relationship.

6.text: The right time to ask for a referral is 2 to 4 weeks after the job
when the customer has lived with the result.
That is the check-in message you are already sending if you have a follow-up system.
Add one line: if you know anyone who could use what we did for you
I would really appreciate the recommendation.

7.text: Referrals are the cheapest customer acquisition channel a local business has access to.
Most businesses skip the ask and spend money on cold audiences instead.
You just have to give them the prompt.
